extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers of machine learning research papers (conference and journal submissions)
extracted.subtask_description: A submission-time checklist to ensure that machine learning papers report sufficient details to allow reproducibility of models, theory, datasets, code, and experimental results. Designed to be used alongside a separate ML code-submission checklist and as part of peer-review/submission workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear description of mathematical setting, algorithm, and/or model
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear description of the mathematical setting, algorithm, and/or model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear explanation of any assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear explanation of any assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of algorithmic complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: An analysis of the complexity (time, space, sample size) of any algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of theoretical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear statement of the claim for any theoretical claim made in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete proofs for theoretical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete proof of the claim for any theoretical claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant dataset statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant statistics, such as number of examples, for all datasets used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train/validation/test split details
rubrics_metrics.description: The details of train / validation / test splits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of excluded data and preprocessing
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of any data that were excluded, and all pre-processing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to downloadable dataset or simulation environment
rubrics_metrics.description: A link to a downloadable version of the dataset or simulation environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of new data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: For new data collected, a complete description of the data collection process, such as instructions to annotators and methods for quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of code dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of dependencies for all shared code related to this work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared training code
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training code as part of the shared code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared evaluation code
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide evaluation code as part of the shared code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared (pre-)trained model(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide (pre-)trained model(s) when sharing code.

rubrics_metrics.name: README with runnable commands and results table
rubrics_metrics.description: README file includes table of results accompanied by precise command to run to produce those results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyper-parameter reporting and selection method
rubrics_metrics.description: The range of hyper-parameters considered, method to select the best hyper-parameter configuration, and specification of all hyper-parameters used to generate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact number of training and evaluation runs
rubrics_metrics.description: The exact number of training and evaluation runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definition of evaluation measures/statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear definition of the specific measure or statistics used to report results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report central tendency and variation
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of results with central tendency (e.g. mean) & variation (e.g. error bars).

rubrics_metrics.name: Runtime or energy cost reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The average runtime for each result, or estimated energy cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computing infrastructure description
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of the computing infrastructure used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist answer fields and usage suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: For each checklist question provide two answer fields: a categorical choice and a free-form comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorical field choices: {Yes, No, Not applicable}. The free-form comment allows authors to provide details when not a clear yes/no or to explain why an item is not applicable. Recommended workflow: require an initial checklist submission earlier in the timeline (e.g., with the abstract) and allow authors to update it up to the paper deadline, given time pressures at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of paper and code artefacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper and the code are separate research artefacts, each with their own checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This checklist (Paper Reproducibility Checklist) is designed to be used simultaneously with the ML Code Submission checklist; treat them as distinct but complementary.
